verdict.rationale: Cursor's docs claim the agent can 'trace how a repo fits together and find the right places to start' (cursor-docs-1), implying automatic codebase mapping without manual file selection, and its agent/codebase indexing generally underlies features like Bugbot and cloud agents that operate across whole repos (cursor-supp-bugbot, cursor-supp-cloud-agents). However, evidence is thin on the specific mechanism (e.g., @codebase search, indexing architecture) or any hands-on account of the agent explaining an unfamiliar codebase end-to-end; the single doc line is a marketing blurb rather than a detailed walkthrough. Missing for 10: concrete documentation or examples of automatic whole-codebase indexing/summarization, hands-on/independent validation that context files needn't be manually selected, and detail on the underlying retrieval mechanism.
